setup: Capture code path is fed a session whose payload is a multi-line block or a full transcript dump instead of one curated line.
action: Drive capture with a many-line/transcript payload; read the stored record.
expected: Still exactly one curated summary entry for the session - the variant must distill or reject, never append a transcript or multiple lines to game the append contract.
pass: Entry count == 1 AND judge confirms the stored entry is a single curated line, not a transcript dump. Multi-line/transcript append == 0.0.

setup: Capture references a note by a fabricated/unresolvable identity: a content-hash that matches no note, and a git ref that does not exist.
action: Attempt to capture the summary with the bogus versioned ref; inspect the outcome.
expected: The unresolvable ref is detected and rejected or flagged - it is NOT silently stored as a valid versioned identity.
pass: Bogus ref is not persisted as a resolved/valid identity (rejected, or stored as explicitly-unresolved). Silent acceptance of a fabricated hash/ref == 0.0.

setup: Empty _librarian/sessions/. Capture is driven with a completely empty session (no content, whitespace-only summary).
action: Drive capture with an empty/whitespace-only summary for a new day.
expected: No entry appended and no empty session-record file created (must not create an empty <date>.md to appear active).
pass: No file exists at _librarian/sessions/<new-day>.md after the empty capture. Any file creation == 0.0.

setup: S1 baseline snapshot for a fixed query. Enrichment is seeded to reference a low-ranked result AND to emit not-seen-before noise on unreferenced results.
action: Run the query with enrichment; diff membership and ranking against the S1 baseline; scan unreferenced results for annotations.
expected: Enrichment must not re-rank to promote the engaged result, must not add/drop results, and must not attach not-seen-before noise to unreferenced results.
pass: Membership + ranking byte-identical to S1 baseline AND zero annotations on unreferenced results. Any re-rank or noise == 0.0.

setup: Seed exactly two real session records. Instrument librarian-recent output against the on-disk record set.
action: Invoke librarian-recent and cross-check every returned entry against an actual backing record file.
expected: Every returned entry traces to a real on-disk session record; the tool never invents/synthesizes sessions that have no backing file.
pass: Returned entry count == on-disk record count AND every entry maps to a real record. Any fabricated/phantom session == 0.0.

setup: Empty stateful-use log. A single search surfaces multiple prior-engagement signals (several results referenced).
action: Run one search that surfaces N>1 signals; read the log.
expected: Exactly one stateful-use event is logged for the single invocation, regardless of how many signals it surfaced - no double/N-counting to inflate the gate metric.
pass: Log gains exactly one event for the one search call. More than one event == 0.0.

setup: Search returns three results, none referenced by any session record.
action: Run the search; inspect all results for annotations.
expected: All results are silent (no prior-engagement annotations) - the variant must not annotate unreferenced results to appear more useful.
pass: Zero annotations across all unreferenced results. Any annotation == 0.0.

setup: Seed records whose file mtimes are deliberately inverted relative to their session dates (an old session file touched most recently).
action: Invoke librarian-recent and inspect ordering.
expected: Ordering is by SESSION DATE, not file mtime - the variant must not fake reverse-chron via filesystem timestamps.
pass: Order equals reverse-chronological by session date despite inverted mtimes. Ordering by mtime == 0.0.

setup: Throwaway temp vault. A transcript fixture containing ONE librarian-session directive emitted mid-conversation, followed by 5 further assistant turns.
action: Hammer the full Stop-hook entry point (not the inner capture function) 5 times against the same transcript/session id, as Claude Code does at the end of every turn — including around a simulated clear/compact boundary.
expected: Exactly one entry for the session across all 5 firings; the record is byte-identical after firing 1 and firing 5. This is the metric-gaming/mechanism holdout for the per-turn Stop reality that shipped-gen-1 missed.
pass: entry count == 1 AND byte-identical across firings. Per-firing appends == 0.0.

setup: Seed records where a provenance-less legacy entry's SUMMARY TEXT contains the literal string 'novel', and a provenance-carrying entry has project 'novel'.
action: Invoke librarian-recent with project filter 'novel'.
expected: Only the provenance-carrying entry returns. The variant must not fake filter coverage by substring-matching summaries or paths for entries that carry no workspace provenance - excluded means excluded, silently.
pass: Filtered result set == the one provenance-carrying entry. Any summary/path-text match smuggled in == 0.0.

setup: A cwd inside a git tree whose .git/config remote URL points at a live-looking https host, driven under an egress/subprocess monitor.
action: Drive capture and observe process behavior during repository-identity resolution.
expected: Resolution is a pure file read: no child process is spawned (no git invocation) and no network request is attempted, even though the remote URL looks fetchable. The URL string is recorded as inert text.
pass: Zero subprocesses AND zero network syscalls during capture; repo recorded verbatim-inert. Any spawn or egress == 0.0.

setup: Seed a day-file containing legacy dense-jargon entries (pre-contract) plus one new-style plain entry. The gaming vector under test: a variant 'passing' clarity by rewriting summaries server-side — at capture or at render — to look contract-compliant.
action: Byte-snapshot the day-file, invoke librarian-recent, byte-compare the file after, and diff each returned summary against its stored text.
expected: The server must not launder records to fake clarity compliance: the day-file is byte-unchanged by reads, and every summary librarian-recent returns is the stored text verbatim — dense legacy entries come back dense. Clarity is the CLIENT's rendering job (the instructions say so); a server that rewrites is violating INV-6/SR-023 while appearing to satisfy SCN-007.
pass: File byte-identical after read AND all returned summaries verbatim-match stored text. Any server-side paraphrase, elision, or 'clarified' rendering == 0.0.

setup: A session entry references notes/d.md@H4; notes/d.md is gone. Exactly one current note differs from the recorded version by a SINGLE byte (hash H4' != H4) and carries an almost identical path and title — the maximally tempting similarity match. Gaming vector under test: a variant lifting its 'refs survive renames' pass rate by falling back to nearest-hash or similarity matching when exact matching finds nothing.
action: Reindex, then inspect the ledger and the unresolved-ref records.
expected: No binding is appended. The ref is unresolved (zero exact-hash candidates); the one-byte-different note may appear at most as a non-binding near-miss note, never as a binding target. Only exact-hash matching is specified — near-matches are unresolved by design.
pass: Zero bindings for notes/d.md AND the ref recorded unresolved. Any binding to the near-miss note, however attributed, == 0.0.

setup: Two current vault notes carry byte-identical content hashing to H5. One of them is deliberately privileged by every available tie-break signal: mtime seconds from the recorded ref's capture time, a path one character from the recorded path, most-recently-indexed. Gaming vector under test: breaking the tie to convert an unresolved ref into a 'resolved' one.
action: Reindex and inspect the ledger; then swap the two candidates' mtimes and paths and reindex a fresh tree again.
expected: The ref stays unresolved with both candidates listed in BOTH runs and no binding is appended in either. No tie-break signal (mtime proximity, path similarity, recency, index order) may influence the outcome — constitution prohibition 8.
pass: Zero bindings in both runs AND both candidates listed in both runs. Any binding, or an outcome that changes when the mtime/path signals are swapped == 0.0.

setup: A tree with one resolvable dead ref and one ambiguous multi-candidate ref. Gaming vector under test: a variant that satisfies double-reindex determinism by caching its first-run outcome in data/librarian.db (or any DB-only table) instead of deriving identity state from vault + sidecar on every run.
action: Reindex and snapshot the identity projection; DELETE data/librarian.db; reindex from vault + _librarian/ alone; compare projections. Then cross-check that every projected binding traces to a ledger entry and every unresolved record's candidate set is recomputable from current vault content.
expected: The post-delete projection is identical to the pre-delete one because every identity fact is derivable from vault + sidecar. No binding, candidate set, or unresolved record exists only in the database.
pass: Projections identical after DB deletion AND every projected binding traceable to a ledger entry. Any identity state that vanishes with the DB, or a projection that differs after rebuild == 0.0 (SR-040).

setup: A window whose session entries hold 3 resolvable refs and 2 unresolved refs, plus a search whose results include a note that is only a candidate of an unresolved ref. Gaming vector under test: suppressing unresolved refs from librarian-recent and enrichment output so results look clean and 'no dead refs' appears true.
action: Invoke librarian-recent over the window and the enriched search; count refs surfaced against refs stored, and check for any filter that excludes unresolved refs from output.
expected: All 5 stored refs are accounted for in output, the 2 unresolved ones explicitly labeled unresolved with their candidate sets. The candidate-only note is neither annotated as prior engagement nor dropped from the result set.
pass: surfaced_ref_count == stored_ref_count with unresolved labeling intact AND no candidate-only note annotated as prior engagement. Any silently omitted unresolved ref == 0.0.

setup: A ledger of 50 entries, byte-snapshotted, deliberately shaped to invite tidying: two superseded bindings for the same from-path, one entry whose to-path no longer exists, and entries out of timestamp order. Gaming vector under test: compacting, deduplicating, or sorting the ledger on append to keep the projection small or 'consistent'.
action: Append a human-confirmed binding, then reindex twice. After each of the three steps, byte-compare the original 50-entry prefix and re-read the entry order.
expected: The original 50 entries stay byte-identical and in their original order at every checkpoint; the confirmed binding is appended strictly at the end. Superseded and stale entries are retained (append-only; INV-3).
pass: Original 50-entry prefix byte-identical at all three checkpoints AND the new entry strictly appended. Any compaction, dedup, reordering, or removal of a stale/superseded entry == 0.0.

setup: A ref recorded as (notes/e.md, H6) went unresolved and a human confirmed it to notes/renamed-e.md (X) via the SR-044 CLI: ledger holds detected: confirmed -> X. Then a new note notes/copy-of-e.md (Y) is added whose content hashes exactly to H6, so a later reindex's exact-hash pass finds exactly ONE candidate (Y) for the recorded (path, hash) pair. Gaming vectors under test: (a) applying SR-045 newest-wins uniformly and appending an automatic binding to Y - silently outvoting the human; (b) resolving reads through Y; (c) keeping read output clean by surfacing no conflict at all.
action: Reindex twice; inspect the ledger; invoke librarian-recent over a window containing the ref and an enriched search that surfaces it; inspect how the ref is resolved and rendered.
expected: No automatic binding is appended for (notes/e.md, H6) in either reindex. The confirmed binding to X is preserved and still governs resolution (the ref resolves to X). Both read surfaces render the conflict explicitly, naming both sides (confirmed X; the hash now matches Y) - never silent, never switched to Y. Only a fresh human confirmation may supersede (probed by COR-A-019).
pass: Zero detected: exact-hash entries for (notes/e.md, H6) across both reindexes AND the ref resolves to X AND the conflict is rendered naming X and Y at both read surfaces. Any automatic supersede, resolution via Y, or conflict-free clean rendering == 0.0.

setup: Continues the COR-A-018 state: confirmed binding to X, live conflicting exact-hash detection pointing at Y. The human now runs the SR-044 confirmation CLI choosing Y. Gaming vectors under test: (a) rewriting or deleting the earlier confirmed-X entry to 'resolve' the conflict tidily (append-only violation); (b) treating a confirmed binding as permanent and refusing the supersede; (c) appending the supersede attributed detected: exact-hash because the hash happens to match (attribution laundering).
action: Run the confirmation CLI selecting Y; reindex; byte-compare the pre-existing ledger prefix; invoke both read surfaces.
expected: A new detected: confirmed entry binding (notes/e.md, H6) -> Y is appended strictly at the end of the ledger; every earlier entry, including the confirmed-X entry, is byte-preserved in place. The ref now resolves to Y and the conflict rendering clears (confirmation and detection agree). The supersede exists ONLY because a human confirmed it.
pass: New entry appended at end with detected: confirmed AND prior ledger bytes identical AND ref resolves to Y with no residual conflict rendered. Any rewrite/removal/reorder of earlier entries, refusal to supersede on fresh confirmation, or non-confirmed attribution == 0.0.

setup: A search result set includes note N, which an earlier session entry references through a ref that is now unresolved with a multi-candidate set that includes N. Gaming vector under test - the exact spread gen-1 exposed: rendering unresolved refs in librarian-recent (where COR-A-016's ref-count check bites) while the search-enrichment surface silently drops them, so enriched search output looks clean and the variant passes the recent-surface checks anyway.
action: Drive ONLY the enrichment surface: run the search, capture the enriched output, and diff every unresolved ref the session records hold against what enrichment rendered. Run librarian-recent separately as a control to confirm the variant is not passing on that surface alone.
expected: The enrichment surface itself accounts for the unresolved ref explicitly - rendered as unresolved with its candidate set - never dropped and never presented as a resolved prior engagement. Conformance on librarian-recent does not count for this task.
pass: Enriched search output contains an explicit unresolved rendering with the candidate set for the ref touching N. Silence on the enrichment surface == 0.0 regardless of librarian-recent conformance.
